name: Akinola Afolarin
bio: Akinola Afolarin is the President & CEO of the Center for Global Sustainability Law (CGSL), where he leads the Center’s global mission to accelerate a just and sustainable transition through law, governance, and policy innovation. His leadership is reflected in CGSL’s commitment to addressing complex environmental and socio‑economic challenges by strengthening the legal and institutional architectures that underpin global sustainability.

Akinola began his legal career more than a decade ago in Nigeria, representing private, corporate, and governmental clients across diverse sectors of the economy. Today, he is recognized as a leading voice in corporate and environmental sustainability law, with core expertise in climate change, corporate sustainability strategy and governance, energy transition, sustainable finance in emerging markets, and the role of the private sector in advancing global climate action.

He is also a Fellow of the Institute for Energy Democracy at the Pace Energy & Climate Center (Pace University), where he contributes significant expertise on energy and climate‑related legal and regulatory issues. His prior experience includes serving as an ESG Specialist at ServiceNow and as Vice Chair of the American Bar Association’s Section on Environment, Energy, and Resources Law (IERL Committee). Akinola is a frequent speaker at conferences and webinars, and his research spans multiple dimensions of corporate and environmental sustainability law.

He earned his LL.B. from Olabisi Onabanjo University and his B.L. from the Nigerian Law School, before pursuing graduate studies at the Elisabeth Haub School of Law at Pace University and the Columbia Climate School/Columbia School of Professional Studies, where he deepened his expertise in international environmental law and sustainability management. He is also a Doctor of Judicial Science (S.J.D.) researcher, examining the structural imbalances embedded within existing climate‑finance frameworks and the legal and equity challenges they create - particularly for countries across sub‑Saharan Africa.
Akinola lives in New York, United States, with his family.

name: Dr. Pianpian Wang
bio: Pianpian is the Chief Operating Officer (COO) at CGSL, overseeing the Center’s operations and the implementation of its strategies towards ensuring efficiency in the actualization of the Center’s vision.

With over thirteen years of experience in environmental law and climate policy, Pianpian Wang brings a distinctive blend of academic rigor and private-sector insight to every engagement. Her expertise spans carbon markets, renewable energy, and corporate sustainability, with a proven track record of helping organizations translate ambitious sustainability goals into actionable strategies.

Pianpian has advised clients across diverse industries—from agile start-ups to global Fortune 500 companies—delivering practical solutions that align with evolving regulations and stakeholder expectations. She believes that business, when guided by responsibility and purpose, can be a powerful catalyst for effective environmental and social governance.

She holds both a Doctor of Juridical Science (S.J.D.) and an LL.M. in Environmental Law and Climate Policy from the Elisabeth Haub School of Law at Pace University, as well as a master’s degree in law from Sun Yat-sen University in China. She is also a certified lawyer in China and a member of the IUCN World Commission on Environmental Law.

name: Maria C. Francois
bio: Maria-Carmelita is excited to join the Center for Global Sustainability Law as its Board Secretary and General Counsel to leverage her legal background and 10 years of boots-on-the-ground success drafting technical and contractual documents. She has managed multimillion-dollar water security, sanitation waste management, and hygiene projects across Africa, the Caribbean, and Pacific Island Countries and Territories, balancing efficiency, legal risk, regulatory compliance, and program goals with environmental, social, and climate risks.

Born and raised in Haiti for the first 13 years of her life, Carmelita learned early how to adapt, rebuild, and navigate complex dynamics with grit, resilience, and integrity. She is fluent in Haitian Creole, English, and French.
Education: Juris Doctor in Law and Master of Arts in International Affairs.
What drives her: designing and executing projects, contracts, strategies, and compliance solutions that improve lives by sustainably reconciling people, profits, and planet.
What grounds her: preserving mental, physical, and spiritual well-being.

name: Priscilla Oche
bio: Priscilla is a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) specialist with a deep commitment to ethical leadership and sustainable development. As Vice President, Governance & Policy at CGSL, she leads the organisation’s efforts to embed transparency, accountability, and strategic foresight into its governance structures.

With a background in legal advisory and regulatory analysis, Priscilla brings clarity and rigour to policy development, ensuring that CGSL’s frameworks align with global best practices while remaining responsive to community needs. Her approach is grounded in collaboration, emotional intelligence, and a belief that good governance is a catalyst for long-term impact.

Priscilla is particularly passionate about integrating sustainability principles into governance processes, advocating for policies that support environmental stewardship, social equity, and resilient institutions. Her work reflects a holistic understanding of compliance as both a technical discipline and a values-driven practice.

name: Abigail Ford
bio: Abigail serves as the Director of Outreach and Communications for CGSL. She brings experience as an ESG analyst, where she has worked on climate data strategy, carbon accounting, policy compliance, and social impact to help companies meet their sustainability goals.

She holds an MSc in International Politics and Human Rights from the London School of Economics and a B.A. in Environmental Studies and International Relations from Tulane University. Her research is broadly focused on the intersection of environmental justice, climate finance and sustainable supply chain management.

name: Jamil Fofanah
bio: Jamil serves as the Regional Director, Law and Policy (Africa) at CGSL where he oversees current developments and tracking of all sustainability-related laws and regulations on the African continent. He is an international criminal and environmental lawyer currently pursuing a doctorate degree in law (S.J.D.) at Pace University’s Elisabeth Haub School of Law, where his research focuses on ecocide and environmental crimes.

Jamil’s practice and scholarship focus on the intersection of international justice, environmental law, and sustainability law. His areas of expertise include international criminal law, climate change, migration, energy law, sports law, business law, human rights, and the connection between global constitutional law and democratic governance.

He has published extensively on these subjects, notably on the intersection of Ecocide and Corporate Law and the relationship between the International Criminal Court (ICC) and Africa. Jamil embodies a unique global perspective, having received advanced legal training in three jurisdictions in Africa, Europe, and North America.
His background also includes experience as a human rights journalist and as a secondary school history and governance administration teacher in Sierra Leone.

name: Shaune Hickson
bio: Shaune is a US-licensed attorney and Fellow at the Center for Global Sustainability Law, where she leads the Center’s work on sustainable investments and other long-term sustainable economic activities across continents in the context of existing and emerging legal frameworks. She is currently pursuing a Master’s in Sustainability and Social Innovation at HEC Paris, with expected graduation in June 2026.

Shaune previously practiced as an Associate Attorney at McLane Middleton, specializing in environmental due diligence and regulatory compliance. Her work included advising clients on facility siting, permitting, and environmental regulatory matters across various sectors.
She serves as Vice Chair of the American Bar Association’s ESG and Sustainability Committee and has contributed research and programming support on a variety of ESG-related topics.
Shaune holds a J.D., and is currently based in Paris, France.

name: Carolina Borges Menezes
bio: Carolina is a fellow at CGSL. As the Fellow, Sustainable Trade Law & Development, her work includes advancing the Center’s initiatives on law, economy, and sustainable development. She is a registered Attorney at the Brazilian Bar Association and currently pursuing a master’s degree in Law and Sustainable Development at Università Degli Studi di Milano, Italy, with a focus on International Trade Law and Regulations, and their impact on promoting economic and Sustainable growth. She is a former member of the International Environmental Law Observatory (OBSDIMA) at the Federal Rural University of Rio de Janeiro. Her background includes research funded by Brazil's National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq) and published work on transnational private regulation and environmental governance.

name: Garrison Jagoe
bio: Garrison is a Research Coordinator at the Center for Global Sustainability Law. He leads a specialized research team and maintains a database of global climate, energy, and biodiversity laws, supporting legal analysis and policy reports. Previously, he produced a report on agroforestry in Kenya with the World Agriculture Forum and coordinated public campaigns with Amnesty International. Garrison is a Master's student in Development Studies, as well as a Bachelor's student in Law at the Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne University, where he also conducted field research and produced a documentary on global food systems. He works fluently in English, French, and Spanish.

name: Tolani Olawore
role: Regional Director, Law & Policy - South America
bio: Tolani provides strategic support to our program development at CGSL. She is a passionate community and programs professional, climate activist, and youth development expert. Currently, she works at the intersection of communications, programs, and community. As a highly skilled community and programs professional, she designs and manages initiatives that empower communities and bridge the gap between passionate individuals and impactful actions. Through her social impact consulting work, she advises organisations on creating sustainable solutions to address social challenges.

Her profound commitment to climate advocacy and community building is evident in her leadership of numerous initiatives aimed at driving positive change. Tolani's work includes leveraging technology for social good, as demonstrated by her professional endeavours with organisations like Wennovation Hub, Opportunity Desk, and the World Economic Forum. Here, she effectively bridges the gap between innovation and meaningful impact.

Tolani is also the founder of Eco-Ed Connect, an organisation dedicated to climate education in schools and raising the next generation of environmental stewards. Under her leadership, Eco-Ed Connect has reached over 11,000 students and trained climate leaders in nine African countries, initiatives supported by the Global Changemakers Grant, among others. She also received an environmental change award at the Global Youth Awards in London, a 25 under 25 nomination from SME100 Africa and serves as a Global Youth Ambassador with TheirWorld and the World Summit Awards, furthering her mission to raise the next generation of environmental stewards.

She holds a Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.) in Structural Engineering from the University of Benin, Nigeria and is currently pursuing a Master’s Degree in International Management at the Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, Morocco, focusing on frameworks for tackling Africa’s urgent development issues.

name: Sophie Price
bio: Sophie Price is a recent graduate of McGill University in Montreal, Canada, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and History with a minor in Environment. Her academic background reflects a distinctly interdisciplinary perspective, bridging global politics, law, and environmental studies. Sophie’s research interests lie at the intersection of international environmental governance, transitional justice and human rights, and the evolving role of international institutions in addressing climate crimes and advancing environmental litigation.

Passionate about the relationship between law and global environmental policy, Sophie aims to pursue a legal education beginning in the fall of 2026. She hopes to contribute to the development of international legal frameworks that promote environmental justice and accountability in the face of climate change.

name: Ategha Bens
bio: Ategha Bens is a Business (Accounting and Finance) lecturer with a deep passion for sustainability and the role of finance in making it a reality. With extensive experience in the business field, Bens thrives on simplifying complex finance and accounting concepts for students in the School of Business, making learning both engaging and practical.

Beyond the classroom, Bens enjoys collaborating with startups on diverse entrepreneurial ventures. As a skilled Financial Modeler, he takes pride in valuing businesses—often involving his students in the process to give them hands-on experience.
Guided by a philosophy that values helping others and fostering teamwork, Bens approaches every project with a collaborative spirit and a commitment to excellence.

name: Caleb Akintola
bio: Caleb is a Data Research intern at the Centre for Global Sustainability Law (CGSL). He has a strong focus on energy efficiency, sustainability, and data-driven problem solving.

At CGSL, he contributes his passion for research, innovation, and data analysis in advancing the organisation’s mission of fostering sustainability at all levels of human needs and creating lasting global impact. He is particularly interested in how technology and energy solutions can be applied to address pressing social and environmental issues.

Outside work, he is committed to continuous learning, exploring clean energy innovations, mentoring peers on sustainability practices and creative pursuits, including graphic design, which he sees as another tool for effective communication and change-making.

name: Iluyemi Joshua
bio: Joshua is a Research Intern at the Center for Global Sustainability Law (CGSL). In this role, he contributes to the mission of the organization through legal research and analysis aimed at clarifying and promoting the critical role of law in fostering a just, equitable, and sustainable global transition.

As a law undergraduate at the University of Lagos, Nigeria, Joshua is passionate about exploring how legal frameworks can drive effective sustainability policies and environmental justice. Through his work with CGSL, he is involved in mapping sustainability-related legal issues, supporting knowledge-sharing initiatives, and contributing to projects that seek innovative legal solutions to global environmental and societal challenges.

Driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and integrity, Joshua believes in the power of law as a transformative tool for sustainable development and is dedicated to advancing a future where prosperity and environmental responsibility coexist harmoniously.

name: Marvellous Omotosho
bio: Marvellous Omotosho is a law graduate from Adekunle Ajasin University, Ondo, Nigeria, and currently works as a legal researcher. He is passionate about emerging legal fields, including space law, animal law, climate law, health law, environmental law, and energy law. With over 15 publications in local and international platforms, he is also a young climate innovator at the Climate Justice Awareness Channel.

name: MD Mahamodul Hasan
bio: MD Mahamodul is an undergraduate law student at the University of Chittagong. His interests span constitutionagl, international, humanitarian, maritime, cyber, and intellectual property law.

Previously, he served as a Research Associate under Professor A.B.M. Abu Noman on an IOM- and YPSA-supported project to develop a victim-of-trafficking (VoT)–centered SOP for law enforcement, conducting stakeholder interviews with judges, police, and survivors. He leads as the Head of Research Wing of the Network for International Law Students (NILS)- Chittagong University Chapter and contributes to Legal Empowerment Bangladesh- LEB’s research team as a Research Associate.

Mahamodul has presented on protecting education in post-conflict societies at the RUEC 1st International Research Conference 2025. His advocacy and research have been recognized with the Best Memorial (Applicant) Award at the BUP National Moot Court Competition 2025, Champion at the 8th NILS Bangladesh Mooting School (2024), and Best Speaker at the NILS CU Public Speaking Competition (2024).

Combining rigorous legal research with public-interest engagement, he aims to advance rule of law solutions that align sustainability, rights protection, and institutional reform in Bangladesh and beyond.

name: Prisca Opara
bio: Prisca is a highly motivated young Nigerian lawyer. She holds a law degree from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, and works with the Law Office of D. Tella Attoni & Co., Rivers State, where her practice focuses on dispute resolution in both civil and criminal matters.

She is also an Associate Member of the Nigerian Institute of Chartered Arbitrators (NICArb) and the Institute of Chartered Mediators and Conciliators (ICMC). Her professional interests include health law and sustainability, reflecting her commitment to exploring legal frameworks that promote social justice and sustainable development.

name: Nwankwere Samuel
bio: Samuel Nwankwere is an Intern at the Center for Global Sustainability Law (CGSL), where he provides IT support and plays a key role in the organization’s digital operations. His responsibilities include managing and maintaining the company website to ensure smooth performance, accessibility, and user-friendliness. In addition, he contributes to branding and visual communication by designing professional materials such as business cards, and other digital assets that reflect CGSL’s identity with clarity and creativity.

Samuel has a foundation in front-end development with skills in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Bootstrap which he applies to create clean, responsive, and functional web solutions. As a graphic designer, he uses Canva effectively for creative projects and is currently expanding his design knowledge by learning Figma. His ability to combine technical expertise with creativity allows him to deliver work that balances functionality with visual appeal.

Known for being a reliable and proactive team player, Samuel is always available to support colleagues and adapt to new challenges. He approaches tasks with enthusiasm, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail. Beyond his current role, Samuel is committed to continuous learning and professional growth, with aspirations to advance in web development, graphic design, and emerging digital technologies.

name: Samuel Abdulkareem
bio: Samuel Abdulkareem is a Sustainability Analyst Intern at the Centre for Global Sustainability Law (CGSL). He is passionate about renewable energy, climate policy, and innovative solutions that drive the global transition to a net-zero future.

At CGSL, he contributes his skills in research and sustainability analysis to support the organisation’s mission of using law and policy as tools for sustainable transformation. He is particularly interested in how finance, technology, and clean energy solutions can be applied to tackle pressing social and environmental challenges across Africa and beyond.

Outside work, he is committed to continuous learning, exploring climate finance innovations, mentoring students on energy and sustainability, and writing on issues at the intersection of policy, technology, and climate.

name: Violet Gagliano
bio: Violet is an intern at the Center for Global Sustainability Law and a junior at Tulane University majoring in Environmental Studies with a minor in Strategy, Leadership, and Analytics. She has a strong academic interest in conservation, environmental policy, and the role of financial systems in addressing climate change and supporting long-term environmental resilience. At CGSL, she contributes to research on sustainable finance law, focusing on ESG disclosure regulation across global jurisdictions. Through this work, she supports CGSL’s mission of advancing legal and policy solutions at the intersection of law, finance, and sustainability.

Outside of work, Violet is deeply passionate about environmental protection and long-term ecological resilience. She is especially interested in initiatives that promote coastal resilience and climate adaptation. She values collaborative engagement with communities and peers to promote the exchange of knowledge on sustainable practices and environmental justice.
